heading: Pioneering compassionate cancer care since 2001
paragraphs: IRCS Cancer Hospital was started in 2001 as a Cancer Detection Centre by the Nellore Red Cross Team, headed by Dr. A.V. Subramanyam, meant for the poor. The land was allotted by the government, and the hospital was inaugurated by Dr. C. Rangarajan, then Governor of Andhra Pradesh.

The first major donation came from J.S. Reddy Charities, which supported the hospital's maintenance for up to a year and a half. Dr. Aruna Chandra Sekharan, a reputed Surgical Oncologist from Adyar Cancer Hospital, then started the Surgical Department — the Operation Theatre, surgical wards, pathology lab and equipment were procured through donations from philanthropists.

The Dodla Vardha Reddy & Rukminamma Charitable Trust funded the Radiation Department building. Radiotherapy services began in 2006 after inauguration by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, then President of India.

The hospital has since grown into a full-fledged cancer therapy centre: a new Surgical Block with twin theatres and a 12-bed ICU (Bhagawan Mahavir Jain Charitable Trust, 2014), a Medical Oncology Department (2019), a new RT Block and Pathology & Biochemistry lab (2022), a Linac Bunker and CT scanner with the ICON Group (2023), and continued equipment donations from philanthropists and organisations including SEIL Energy India.

Experienced Surgical, Radiation and Medical Oncologists serve patients from four districts — Nellore, Prakasam, Chittoor and Kadapa — and beyond. The Indian Red Cross continues to support the hospital, which also runs an Annaprasadam food scheme for inpatients and regular cancer awareness programs in schools, colleges and villages.
